questions.text: Under CIAP Document 102 Article 20.08, when must the contractor give written notice for a claim for extra cost?

options.text: Within fifteen days after receipt of the instruction, drawings, or specifications involving a change
Only after final payment
Within fifteen years after completion
Only after the owner files arbitration

rationale.correct: CIAP Document 102 requires written notice within fifteen days after receipt of the instruction, drawings, or specifications involving a change.
rationale.takeaway: CIAP Document 102 requires written notice within fifteen days after receipt of the instruction, drawings, or specifications involving a change.

questions.text: If delay is attributable to owner-supplied materials or delayed owner decisions, when is written notice required under CIAP Document 102?

options.text: Within fifteen days after recognition of the delay
Only after the whole project is completed
Only if the owner admits fault
Never, because delay claims are automatic

rationale.correct: CIAP Document 102 requires written notice within fifteen days after recognition of owner-attributable delay.
rationale.takeaway: CIAP Document 102 requires written notice within fifteen days after recognition of owner-attributable delay.

questions.text: Which situation is the express exception to giving extra-cost notice before proceeding?

options.text: Emergency endangering life or property
The contractor prefers speed
The owner is absent from a site meeting
The work is aesthetically important

rationale.correct: The checked provisions recognize an emergency endangering life or property as the exception.
rationale.takeaway: The checked provisions recognize an emergency endangering life or property as the exception.

questions.text: When extra work is valued by actual direct cost under CIAP Document 102, what must the contractor present?

options.text: A correct cost account with vouchers and supporting documents
Only a verbal estimate
Only a photograph of the work
A final payment receipt only

rationale.correct: CIAP Document 102 requires a correct account of direct cost with vouchers and supporting documents.
rationale.takeaway: CIAP Document 102 requires a correct account of direct cost with vouchers and supporting documents.

questions.text: What actual-direct-cost formula is supported by CIAP Document 102 for extra work?

options.text: Actual direct cost plus VAT if any plus fifteen percent for contractor profit and overhead
Actual direct cost plus fifty percent automatically
Owner estimate only
Architect fee plus contractor equipment only

rationale.correct: The source states actual direct cost plus VAT if any plus fifteen percent for profit and overhead.
rationale.takeaway: The source states actual direct cost plus VAT if any plus fifteen percent for profit and overhead.

questions.text: What is the architect-linked role in UAP Document 301 when claims or contract interpretation issues arise?

options.text: Make decisions on claims and matters relating to execution, progress, or interpretation within the contract framework
Ignore all claims until litigation
Guarantee contractor profit
Replace the contract documents with oral instructions

rationale.correct: UAP Document 301 gives the architect a decision role on claims and contract interpretation matters.
rationale.takeaway: UAP Document 301 gives the architect a decision role on claims and contract interpretation matters.

questions.text: Which claim is not automatically waived by acceptance of final payment under CIAP Document 102?

options.text: A claim covered by prior notice and reserved for filing under the contract
A completely unrecorded claim raised for the first time after final payment
A claim the contractor intentionally abandoned
A claim unsupported by any contract notice

rationale.correct: CIAP Document 102 preserves claims with prior notice and reservation, pending unresolved claims, arbitrated disputes, and claims acknowledged by the owner as outside final payment.
rationale.takeaway: CIAP Document 102 preserves claims with prior notice and reservation, pending unresolved claims, arbitrated disputes, and claims acknowledged by the owner as outside final payment.

questions.text: If an unresolved construction contract dispute arises under CIAP Document 102, what is the source-supported dispute path?

options.text: File a claim with CIAC for arbitration under EO 1008 construction arbitration rules
Ask a supplier to decide
Treat the dispute as waived without checking the contract
Use only a social media announcement

rationale.correct: CIAP Document 102 sends unresolved connected disputes to arbitration and filing with CIAC.
rationale.takeaway: CIAP Document 102 sends unresolved connected disputes to arbitration and filing with CIAC.

questions.text: A contractor submits an extra-cost claim saying only that costs were significant. What is missing for a source-safe review?

options.text: Written notice, contract basis, and cost support such as vouchers or other supporting documents
Only a project photograph
Only a future promise to explain later
Only the contractor signature

rationale.correct: The checked sources require written notice and direct-cost support rather than assertion alone.
rationale.takeaway: The checked sources require written notice and direct-cost support rather than assertion alone.

questions.text: What is the safest workflow for a construction claim question?

options.text: Check notice, entitlement, cost or time proof, contract decision path, and arbitration if unresolved
Approve every claimed amount immediately
Ignore written deadlines
Wait until final payment and then decide from memory

rationale.correct: The workflow follows the source-supported notice, proof, decision, and dispute path.
rationale.takeaway: The workflow follows the source-supported notice, proof, decision, and dispute path.
